Headset mode (split screen for the two lenses). Turn off to preview on the phone alone.
Scan a new viewer QR code
Google Cardboard (default). Scan the QR code on your viewer for a better picture.

After pressing Start, put the phone into the headset. A dot in the middle of your view is your pointer: keep it on a button for 2 seconds to click it, or click with a mouse. Look down to bring up the control bar (it stays up while paused).

Viewer button or mouse click anywhere else: play / pause. Press twice quickly: recenter.
Volume up / down keys: skip forward / back.
Change the dot and look time in Settings > Pointer.

Percent, up to 400% for a giant IMAX-style screen. For 360° video this zooms in on the picture.
In tenths of a metre (30 = 3 m). The picture keeps the same apparent size; only the depth feeling changes. Use zoom to change the size.
Moves the screen up (+) or down (−), in degrees. Not used for 360° video.
Off: the phone keeps its normal brightness. On: use the level below while a video is playing.
Half: the two pictures are squeezed to fit one frame (most common). Full: two complete pictures. Automatic guesses from the video shape.
Turn on if the 3D looks inside-out.
%1$s\n\nTap to scan a viewer QR code. The viewer is remembered until you scan another.

Moves the left and right pictures apart (+) or together (−). Use it if the picture feels slightly off or you see double, for example because your eyes are further apart or closer than your viewer\'s lenses.

Focus is set by the lenses in your viewer, so an app cannot change it. A sharper-looking picture needs a viewer with focus adjustment, or you can wear your glasses (the screen distance and zoom settings do not change focus). Some viewers also take clip-in prescription lenses.
How far the volume buttons jump forward or back.
For viewers without a button that touches the screen: the video starts by itself after a delay.
A language code such as en, de or hi. Leave empty to use the video\'s default.
Uses subtitles inside the video or a subtitle file you add on the start screen.
Moves captions up (+) or down (−), as a percentage of the screen height.
Back to the default values. Your viewer profile is kept.
Show the dot in the middle of the view
A small dot that shows where you are pointing inside the headset.
Keep the dot on an in-headset button and it clicks by itself. Turn off to click only with the mouse or a tap.

I was looking for a free VR video player with advanced features for my phone-in-headset viewer, but I could not find one, so I made my own. It plays 2D, 3D and 360° videos from files or links, and it is fully customisable.
Have a feature request or found a bug? Write to me:

This app is built with free software. Thank you to the people behind it:

• Google Cardboard SDK (head tracking, lens correction, viewer QR codes). Apache License 2.0. github.com/googlevr/cardboard

• AndroidX Media3 / ExoPlayer (video playback). Apache License 2.0. developer.android.com/media/media3

• AndroidX AppCompat and Preference libraries. Apache License 2.0.

• Material Components for Android (buttons, cards, theme). Apache License 2.0.

• Material Icons by Google (the start screen icons). Apache License 2.0.

• Protocol Buffers (lite), used by the Cardboard SDK. BSD 3-Clause licence.

Moves the bar in the headset down (−) or up (+), in degrees. Lower it so you do not see it when you tilt your head a little.

The lenses bend the picture, so a mouse click can land beside the pointer, more so near the edges. Raise this if clicks land too far from the middle than the pointer; lower it if too near. 100 is the normal setting.
